q: Compared with lactate fermentation in humans, alcoholic fermentation in yeast…
options: also regenerates NAD+ and yields 2 ATP per glucose, but releases CO2 and produces ethanol
produces more ATP per glucose, because removing CO2 from pyruvate releases extra energy
doesn't need NAD+ regeneration at all, because yeast cells use FAD as their carrier instead
produces lactate and CO2, and is easily reversed once oxygen becomes available again
explanation: Both pathways solve the same problem – regenerating NAD+ so glycolysis can continue – and both yield only glycolysis's net 2 ATP. Yeast decarboxylates pyruvate to ethanal (releasing CO2), then reduces ethanal to ethanol using NADH. The CO2 makes bread rise and the ethanol is used in brewing; because CO2 is lost, the yeast pathway isn't readily reversible.
